disposition_reason: Table 2 prints mean ± SD, minimum and maximum cadmium and mercury for five dairy product categories bought in six Vietnamese cities.

study.design: multi-city retail survey of 367 milk and dairy samples (114 liquid milk, 158 yogurt, 21 cheese, 44 milk cake, 30 milk powder)
study.origin: produced and processed in Vietnam (per conclusion); brands not named
study.market: stores, markets and supermarkets in Ha Noi, Hai Phong, Da Nang, Buon Ma Thuot, Ho Chi Minh City and Can Tho, Vietnam
study.method: microwave digestion HNO3/H2SO4/HClO4 (10:1:1) + H2O2; flame AAS for Cd, cold-vapor AAS for Hg (Hitachi AZ3000)
study.qa: spike recoveries Cd 93.0-94.02%, Hg 92.5-95.5% (Table 1); procedural blanks; five replicate measurements

unresolved: Pooled all-dairy statistics (Table 3: Cd 62.99 ± 140.45, Hg 27.59 ± 25.35 ppb) are cross-product summaries and not recorded.
Table 1 prints mercury 'level found' 191 ppb for a 2 ppb spike while the recovery is 95.5%; likely a typo for 1.91.

Several authors (Nguyen CV, Tran KV, Dinh HTD) also wrote the 2021 Ho Chi Minh City cheese survey (60 products, Nov 2019-Sep 2020); the 21 cheese samples here have different n and values and are not a reprint, but overlapping samples cannot be excluded.
Detection counts (Cd 139/367, Hg 271/367) not recorded as findings.
